title: Count Triplets with Even XOR Set Bits II
summary: Count triplets from arrays a, b, and c where the bitwise XOR of each triplet has an even number of set bits.
statement: Count triplets from arrays a, b, and c where the bitwise XOR of each triplet has an even number of set bits.
constraints: a, b, and c are nonempty arrays of nonnegative integers.
Choose one value from each array and count index triplets whose XOR has an even number of set bits.
Repeated equal values at different indices count as separate choices.
hints: Popcount parity of an XOR equals the XOR of the operands’ popcount parities.
Count even- and odd-popcount values in each array, then multiply the four parity combinations totaling even.
Add EEE, EOO, OEO, and OOE products.
These four disjoint parity patterns are exactly the triples with parity XOR zero, and frequency products count their index choices.
editorial: These four disjoint parity patterns are exactly the triples with parity XOR zero, and frequency products count their index choices.

tests.explanation: The XOR is zero, which has zero set bits and therefore counts.
Classifying each number by set-bit parity counts the combinations whose three parities XOR to even.
